R-08/R-58 (the fabricated FAILED badge, killed at the source): added `close_state_for(plan, decisive, last_result_ok)` — GD-10's predicate verbatim — and routed all three close sites through it (sequenced close, settle pass, run_outcome). New `last_result_ok` state is recorded from every result. A verdict-less non-failing plan now closes `done` with detail "(closed, no verdict)" via `close_detail()`. The sequenced "new plan closes the previous one" heuristic is gated on `orch-config.json "strategy" == "serial"`; `run_outcome` folds every plan to its effective close state (so a research-shaped run finally closes at all — the old rule returned None forever), excludes the reserved `orchestrator` card, and stays None while any agent runs. A terminal badge now reopens from `failed` as well as `done`. Final-gate decision text is keyed on `(plan, role)` (new `MAX_FINALGATE_ATTEMPTS`, config key `max_finalgate_attempts`) so `plan=finalgate role=test` says "PASS -> run complete" / "FAIL -> spawn fixer, re-gate N/2" and never names a critique. R-23 (`tailer.py`): pure `tail_once(path, Checkpoint)` plus a small `Tailer` wrapper. Checkpoint is a frozen `(st_dev, st_ino, size, offset, line_no, gen, mtime_ns)` value; `fresh`/`rotated`/**`shrunk` (`size < offset` explicit — the RUNSTATE-15 branch)** each force a re-ingest from 0 and bump `gen` (SD-10 signal; the GD-26 sweep stays mirror.py's). Torn tails cut at the last `\n` with the remainder deferred; stat-first short circuit returns without opening the file; every line carries 1-based `line_no` + absolute `byte_offset` (incl. blank lines, so GD-24/R-47 positional ids never shift); `read_cap` bounds one read (`more=True`); `.compact.tmp.*` defers a tick with a 60 s staleness escape; a vanished file never resets a checkpoint. Equal-size in-place rewrite is documented as not-re-ingested by default with an opt-in `resync_on_mtime_only`.

R-24 (`store.py`): `.touch/` touch-events-v2 append-only store, D5 layout (`sessions/<key>/events.jsonl`, `runs/<runId>/events.jsonl`, `custom-state.jsonl`, `control.jsonl`), root from arg > `$TOUCH_STATE_DIR` > `<repo>/.touch`, dirs 0700, path components percent-escaped and exactly reversible via `streams()`. Fixed key order `v,seq,ts,source,provenance,kind,ref,data` (no `stream` field — that is mongo_store's addition). Per-stream `seq` resumed from the file at boot as `max(line count, highest stored seq)+1` and **re-derived inside the flock whenever the file grew behind our back**, so even out-of-contract concurrent writers get unique seqs (4 processes x 100 appends → 400 records, 0 torn, seqs 1..400). One `flock`'d `write()` per batch; a torn tail is terminated with a newline (never deleted) and counted; oversize (>1 MiB) records are stubbed `{oversize,bytes,keys}` rather than dropped or raised. `validate_ref` implements GD-11's union + GD-11(d)'s `{root,name,attempt}`/`{task,plan,stage?,attempt?}`, rejects malformed known shapes (non-17-hex agentId, non-UUID uuid, string `ordinal`/`pid`, **int `procStart`**), exempts `legacy:<task>:<id8>`, and retains unknown shapes verbatim. Token records get all four keys; `provenance` is a required keyword from the closed five-value enum with `custom-state`/`control` pinned to `{asserted,touch}`; `kind`/`source` are slug-validated but open at the tail so R-52 rides this machinery with store.py unchanged; `custom-state`/`control` fsync. Cursors are `<stream>#<seq:012d>` (`cursor_key`/`parse_cursor_key`, bare seq rejected), plus `read_since`, `read_from_cursor`, and incremental `follow()` over the tailer. No reducer here (GD-23) — a test guards the exported surface by name.

R-29 (`ws.py`): pure RFC 6455 codec, no socket/asyncio import (asserted via AST). `accept_key` (RFC §1.3 vector), `encode_frame`/text/binary/ping/pong/close, big-int `mask_bytes`, `decode_frame` returning `(None,0)` on a partial frame, and `FrameDecoder` with continuation reassembly, control frames interleaved mid-message, UTF-8 validation, and size caps. Violations map to RFC §7.4.1 close codes: 1002 (RSV, unknown opcode, fragmented/oversize control frame, wrong masking direction, non-minimal length, stray continuation, new data frame mid-message, 1-byte/reserved close code), 1007 (bad UTF-8 in text or close reason), 1009 (over cap, refused from the header before buffering). The prior art's skip-and-discard path is kept as `drain_frames` and asserted **byte-for-byte against the real `monitor_server.parse_client_frames`**, which satisfies R-29's "masked client frames dropped unread" while T3's unmasking codec exists alongside.

impl.summary:
sp-refs-mongostore (R-43 + R-44) implemented in four new files, all owned by this sub-plan; nothing else was touched.

aggregator/refs.py (R-43) — the single `ref_key()` canonicalizer. One `_Spec` table covers all 18 kinds of GD-24's grammar (the 7 GD-11 union members plus every collection id); keys are pure functions of ref *values*, so insertion order can never produce two documents. Percent-escaping of `% # | :` in user-chosen components (single pass both ways, `%2525` → `%25`), zero-padding for the *ordering* ints only (seq 12 / lineNo 8 / ordinal 4 / attempt 3, pid deliberately unpadded), field-name-keyed BSON type pins (procStart string, pid/ordinal/seq int, bool excluded), control-char and length caps. `canonical_ref()` emits the fixed-order `ref{kind,…}` sub-document, `ref_id()` returns None for unknown shapes and for groupings that name no document (`toolUseId`, `orchAgent`, `legacyPlan`), `parse_ref_key()` is the proven inverse of every grammar. Explicit `kind` is required wherever key sets collide (`{stream,seq}` is both `events` and `custom_state_events`) — GD-12's no-guessing rule. `legacy_agent_id(task, id8)` is the one escaping entry point for GD-14 legacy agent ids; an unescaped one is rejected. Module is pure: imports only `re`.

aggregator/mongo_store.py (R-44) — GD-24's table as `COLLECTIONS` (15 specs: id kind, required fields, bsonType pins, provenance enum, indexes, accumulable/set fields, declared `_raw` paths), `$jsonSchema` builders pinning `_id` to bsonType string on every collection, index bootstrap with `index_def()` that *refuses* `expireAfterSeconds` structurally (GD-26). Algebra: `$max/$min/$addToSet/$setOnInsert` plus `$set` fenced off accumulable fields; `$inc`/`$push`/`$unset`/etc. refused with the reason in the message; `merge_ops` catches a field under two operators before the server does. `apply_update`/`apply_operations`/`fingerprint`/`counts` are the in-memory twin of the server's upsert (BSON canonical type order reproduced) — that's what makes GD-25's acceptance test runnable with no database. Plus `_raw` wrapping (declared paths always, undeclared hostile subtrees auto-wrapped and marked `_rawAuto`), >8 MB oversize stub, `ts_fields()` (Date + tsRaw, ms truncation, no clock anywhere), `check_id()` proving every `_id` round-trips through `refs.ref_key`, lazy-pymongo `open_client/ping/ensure_schema/bulk_upsert/classify_write_errors` (writeErrors always inspected, duplicate keys counted per GD-29), and `CLIENT_OPTIONS` stated once for mirror.py.

Tests (stdlib only, standalone executables, picked up by tests/run_all.sh):
- tests/test_refs.py — 100+ checks: every kind built in up to 6 insertion orders ⇒ one `_id` and one byte-stable ref doc; parse round-trip per kind; escaping round-trips a task name containing `#|:%`; type pins both arms; padding == numeric order; unknown shapes retained/never keyed; `ref_key` proven **byte-identical to store.cursor_key** (the proof store.py:400 hands to this sub-plan); the GD-11 union agrees with `store.REF_SHAPES` shape-for-shape; AST purity guard.

Fixed by splitting the guarded path: (1) the conditional update now runs with `upsert=False`, so it can never insert; (2) on no match, when `upsert`, a create is attempted only if `apply_update(None, …)` yields a document carrying the collection's required fields (a payload-only write is not a create → `acquired: False`, nothing written, no round trip wasted), and the create is an explicit `insert_one`, so "already exists" comes back as the duplicate key GD-29 requires be counted (`tolerated_dups: 1`). Added `_guard_lost()` and `_driver_error()`; the latter maps `DOCUMENT_VALIDATION_FAILED` (121) to `SchemaError` rather than `MongoUnavailable`, so a `$jsonSchema` refusal can never feed GD-30's breaker. Both of the critique's live reproductions now return the documented result: payload-only late custom-state write → `{acquired: False, tolerated_dups: 0}`, head untouched; expiry-only lease renewal by a non-holder → same, holder untouched; by the holder → `{acquired: True, matched: 1}` (re-verified independently against mongo:7, plus new unit and live assertions).
